pages.title: FSMap and MDSMap: cluster map, MDS states, compat sets, fs/mds commands

features.name: FSMap multi-filesystem cluster map
features.description: Monitor-owned Paxos-versioned map of all file systems (fscid -> Filesystem{MDSMap, MirrorInfo}), the shared standby pool, mds_roles, standby_epochs, default_compat, legacy_client_fscid, enable_multiple. One FSMap epoch per committed proposal.
features.notes: Produced only by the unmodified MDSMonitor; the Rust MDS consumes it.

features.name: Per-filesystem MDSMap
features.description: Per-fs projection consumed by MDS daemons and clients: ranks (in/up/failed/stopped/damaged), mds_info of rank holders and standby-replay followers, flags, pools, session timeouts, max sizes, required client features, balancer settings, quiesce DB membership, compat.
features.notes: Native encoding struct_v 5 / ev 20; mds_info_t v10. libcephfs uses the C++ decoder, the kernel a partial one.

features.name: MDS daemon and rank state machine
features.description: Numeric states (DNE 0, STOPPED -1, BOOT -4, STANDBY -5, CREATING -6, STARTING -7, STANDBY_REPLAY -8, REPLAY 8, RESOLVE 9, RECONNECT 10, REJOIN 11, CLIENTREPLAY 12, ACTIVE 13, STOPPING 14, DAMAGED 15) and the legal transition table enforced by the mon for beacons and by the C++ MDS for maps.
features.notes: Mon imposes CREATING/STARTING/REPLAY/STANDBY_REPLAY/STOPPING; the MDS requests the rest via beacon.

features.name: Rank sets and implicit rank states
features.description: in/up/failed/stopped/damaged sets; implicit FAILED/STOPPED/DAMAGED/DNE for ranks without holder; derived predicates is_degraded, is_resizeable, is_followable, is_resolving, is_rejoining, get_recovery_mds_set.
features.notes: Multi-rank recovery barriers are expressed through these predicates on the MDSMap.

features.name: CompatSet feature gating
features.description: Daemon compat (from boot beacon) vs fs compat (default_compat at creation). A standby is eligible only if its incompat/ro_compat masks are a superset of the fs's (writeable), and, unless the fs is upgradeable, the fs's masks are a superset of the standby's. Plain compat bits are ignored.
features.notes: The only hard mechanism that keeps incompatible MDS implementations off a file system.

features.name: Upgradeable compat merge on promotion
features.description: When a standby with extra incompat/ro_compat bits is promoted into an upgradeable fs (no ranks in, or single rank / all failed with standby-replay disabled), the fs compat permanently merges the standby's features.
features.notes: Tested by qa/tasks/cephfs/test_admin.py:1407 (test_standby_incompat_upgrade) and :1419 (test_standby_replay_not_upgradeable).

features.name: Forced INLINE incompat bit and compat bootstrap
features.description: Incompat 7 'mds uses inline data' is force-inserted into every stored daemon compat and fs compat; an empty boot compat is replaced by the v16.2.4 set; mds_info_t < v10 decodes with the v16.2.4 set.
features.notes: A daemon whose beacons omit bit 7 fails the beacon compat equality check.

features.name: Beacon compat immutability
features.description: Every non-boot beacon that reaches prepare_beacon must carry a CompatSet equal (masks) to the stored one; otherwise the daemon is failed (blocklisted if it holds a rank).

features.name: Standby pool and standby selection scoring
features.description: get_available_standby scans standbys in gid order, skips laggy/frozen/incompatible ones, scores by mds_join_fs affinity (match > vanilla > other fs) combined with host anti-affinity (any different-host candidate beats any same-host candidate), ties to lowest gid.

features.name: mds_join_fs affinity
features.description: Daemons advertise a preferred fs name in each beacon; the mon resolves it to join_fscid (NONE if unknown) and uses it for selection and for affinity-driven swaps.

features.name: refuse_standby_for_another_fs flag
features.description: When set on a fs, standbys whose join_fscid names another fs are never selected for it; vanilla standbys still are.
features.notes: Soft isolation layer only.

features.name: Standby-replay assignment
features.description: With allow_standby_replay and a resizeable fs, the mon assigns standbys as STANDBY_REPLAY followers of followable ranks; followers are preferred replacements (unless frozen, which blocks replacement).
features.notes: Disallowing it is required for an fs to be upgradeable with ranks in.

features.name: Failed-rank replacement and laggy handling
features.description: Failed ranks are filled by find_replacement_for + promote (REPLAY); laggy holders are replaced only if a replacement exists and the fs is joinable; otherwise they stay up with laggy_since.
features.notes: Detail of beacon timing in beacon-and-monitor.md.

features.name: Affinity-driven swaps
features.description: Per tick and fs, at most one daemon with weaker join_fscid affinity is failed (SR) or failed over (active) in favour of a better-affinity standby.
features.notes: Causes failovers of healthy actives.

features.name: max_mds resize
features.description: Grow: lowest missing rank promoted (CREATING if never existed, STARTING if in stopped), one per tick when resizeable and joinable. Shrink: rank size(in)-1 set to STOPPING if ACTIVE; MDS reports STOPPED; mon removes the rank into stopped.

features.name: fs new
features.description: Create a fs from pools with validation (_check_pool, empty metadata pool, overlay, enable_multiple, --fscid with --force), apply --set options, tag pool applications, set metadata pool opts, assign standbys immediately (CREATING) unless --recover.
features.notes: Initial assignment ignores NOT_JOINABLE.

features.name: fs rm
features.description: Remove an offline fs (no rank up), fail remaining standby-replay daemons, clear default fs if it was this one, reset join_fscid references.

features.name: fs fail and joinable flag
features.description: fs fail sets NOT_JOINABLE and fails every daemon of the fs (holders blocklisted); joinable true/false toggles NOT_JOINABLE; fs set max_mds also clears it.

features.name: fs reset
features.description: Disaster recovery: replace the fs by a fresh MDSMap with rank 0 failed (REPLAY next), other former ranks stopped, settings, flags (including NOT_JOINABLE) and mirror info reset to defaults, compat = default_compat.
features.notes: Leaves MDSMap epoch 0 until next modification (inferred). Does not fail remaining standby-replay daemons, whose mds_roles entry then has no mds_info and fails sanity() (inferred).

features.name: fs set down
features.description: down true saves max_mds in old_max_mds and sets max_mds 0 (all ranks stopped); down false restores old_max_mds or 1.

features.name: Session timeout and autoclose
features.description: session_timeout (default 60 s, min 30) and session_autoclose (default 300 s, min 30) in the MDSMap drive MDS stale/evict logic and client renew cadence (kclient timeout/4, libcephfs timeout/3) and Ganesha delegation timeout bound.

features.name: max_file_size
features.description: Maximum file size (default 1 TiB, min 65536) published in the MDSMap; kclient caps s_maxbytes, libcephfs checks writes/truncates.

features.name: max_xattr_size
features.description: Maximum xattr blob size (default 64 KiB); MDS returns ENOSPC beyond it; kclient buffers setxattr under Xx only within it (ev >= 18).
features.notes: No range check on fs set.

features.name: allow_new_snaps flag
features.description: CEPH_MDSMAP_ALLOW_SNAPS (default on); MDS rejects mksnap with EPERM when clear, after waiting for the client's mdsmap epoch.

features.name: allow_multimds_snaps (MDS-issued)
features.description: Flag the MDS sets itself (mon command with confirm=--yes-i-am-really-a-mds) once old pre-mimic snapshots are gone; gates max_mds > 1 for filesystems that ever had snapshots; health MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS.
features.notes: Default on for new filesystems.

features.name: refuse_client_session flag
features.description: Flag making the MDS reject new sessions and reconnects; libcephfs refuses to mount (EACCES); kclient does not read flags and only sees MDS rejects; required for fs rename/swap.

features.name: inline_data (deprecated)
features.description: Per-fs inline data enable flag (enable requires --yes-i-really-really-mean-it); health FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED.

features.name: Balancer settings in the map
features.description: balancer (Mantle object name), bal_rank_mask (hex rank mask, -1/all, 0/0x0), balance_automate flag (default off) carried in the MDSMap and consumed by the MDS balancer.

features.name: standby_count_wanted and insufficient-standby health
features.description: Per-fs desired number of standbys (default -1, auto-set to 1); MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY counts the shared pool plus the fs's standby-replay daemons.

features.name: standby_enable_host_anti_affinity
features.description: Per-fs switch (default true) for preferring standbys on a different host than the rank holder being replaced/followed.

features.name: required_client_features / min_compat_client
features.description: Bitset of CEPHFS_FEATURE_* bits clients must support; the MDS evicts sessions lacking them when the set changes; fs set min_compat_client (deprecated) replaces the whole set with the single bit of that release (empty for releases before jewel).
features.notes: Kernel mis-skips the encoded field when non-empty (inferred).

features.name: Data pools management
features.description: fs add_data_pool / rm_data_pool maintain data_pools (first = default, cannot be removed); clients validate layouts against it; statfs reports the single pool when only one exists.

features.name: Default (legacy) file system
features.description: legacy_client_fscid: set to the first fs created or via fs set-default; unqualified 'mdsmap' subscriptions and rank-only roles resolve to it.

features.name: fs rename and fs swap
features.description: Rename (or swap names and optionally fscids of) offline filesystems with refuse_client_session set and mirroring disabled; pool application tags rewritten.
features.notes: kclient with old mds_namespace fails map decode and unmounts.

features.name: fs compat / mds compat commands
features.description: fs compat add/rm compat|incompat edits one fs compat when no rank is up; deprecated mds compat rm_* edits default_compat; fs compat show / mds compat show display them.
features.notes: Feature id >= 64 asserts the monitor (inferred). With no rank up but standby-replay daemons still attached (mds fail while not joinable), add_incompat fails sanity() at commit and rm_incompat later makes promote() assert is_upgradeable() when the SR is promoted (both inferred from code). fs compat show needs 'mds r'.

features.name: Mirroring metadata (MirrorInfo)
features.description: fs mirror enable/disable/peer_add/peer_remove store mirroring state and peers in the Filesystem; consumed by cephfs-mirror through the fsmap subscription.

features.name: enable_multiple flag
features.description: fs flag set enable_multiple controls creation of more than one fs (default true).

features.name: mds fail with blocklisting
features.description: Fail a daemon by role, gid or name: rank holders (not SR) are blocklisted for mon_mds_blocklist_interval, rank moves to failed and is replaced next tick; standbys/SR are just removed.

features.name: Damaged ranks and mds repaired
features.description: A DAMAGED beacon (from the holder or its standby-replay follower) blocklists the holder, fails the follower, moves the rank to damaged; mds repaired moves it back to failed.
features.notes: Clients treat damaged as unavailable.

features.name: Debug/admin rank commands (mds rm, rmfailed, freeze, set_state)
features.description: mds rm removes non-rank daemons without blocklist; mds rmfailed drops a rank from failed; mds freeze sets FROZEN (never selected, never dropped, blocks replacement if SR); mds set_state writes any state.
features.notes: mds set_state accepts only 0..20, so on a standby gid it trips the STANDBY assert in FSMap::modify_daemon and aborts the leader monitor (inferred). mds rm accepts any state <= 0, including CREATING/STARTING rank holders, without blocklisting. mds rmfailed leaves a rank in 'in' that is never replaced (inferred).

features.name: Read-only fs/mds commands
features.description: fs dump [epoch], fs get, fs ls, fs lsflags, fs feature ls, fs compat show, mds stat, mds metadata, mds versions, mds count-metadata, mds last-seen, mds ok-to-stop; JSON layouts consumed by mgr/orchestrators.
features.notes: mds ok-to-stop used by orchestrators (cephadm/rook) (unverified for this page).

features.name: Map subscriptions and null maps
features.description: Subscriptions fsmap, fsmap.user, mdsmap, mdsmap.<fscid> (cap 'mds r'); MDS sessions identified by addrs receive their fs map or a standby null map (default MDSMap: empty compat, enabled false, fs_name 'cephfs', own mds_info only, epoch = standby_epochs[gid]); unknown/evicted daemons and daemons whose STOPPED beacon committed get a null map with epoch UINT32_MAX.

features.name: FSMapUser name directory
features.description: Small map (epoch, legacy fscid, list of fscid/name) used by clients mounting by fs name before subscribing to mdsmap.<fscid>.

features.name: Kernel partial MDSMap decode
features.description: kclient reads epoch, timeouts, max sizes, max_mds, mds_info (rank, inc, state>0, addr, laggy, export_targets), data pools, in (possible_max_rank), enabled, fs_name (checked vs mds_namespace), damaged count, max_xattr_size; skips the rest.
features.notes: State <= 0 entries (standby-replay followers, CREATING and STARTING holders) are invisible; flags are read into an unused field; required_client_features is mis-skipped when non-empty (inferred).

features.name: Client-side availability check and mount gating
features.description: libcephfs-based clients decode the full MDSMap. Client::mount checks is_cluster_available (TRANSIENT waits, STUCK fails with CEPH_FUSE_NO_MDS_UP) only when require_mds is set: ceph-fuse passes fuse_require_active_mds (default true), libcephfs ceph_mount passes false. REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION makes every Client::mount fail with EACCES before contacting an MDS.

features.name: MDSMap epoch gating of client requests
features.description: Client requests carry mdsmap_epoch; the MDS waits for its own map to reach that epoch before validating pools in layouts and before mksnap.

features.name: Export targets publication
features.description: MDS sends MMDSLoadTargets with ranks it exports to; stored in mds_info.export_targets; kclient/libcephfs pre-open sessions and send reconnects to export targets.

features.name: last_failure_osd_epoch fencing barrier
features.description: When a rank holder is failed the mon blocklists it and records the OSDMap epoch; a replacement waits for that OSDMap epoch before replay or standby-replay takeover.
features.notes: Overwritten on every erase of a daemon attached to the fs; callers that do not blocklist (SR removal, mds rm, stop) write 0. fs fail fails daemons in ascending gid order, so an SR with a higher gid than its holder resets the value to 0 after the holder's blocklist (inferred).

features.name: Incarnation
features.description: mds_info.inc = FSMap epoch at promotion; C++ MDS uses it as Objecter client incarnation; libcephfs detects restarts via incarnation change.

features.name: Quiesce DB membership in MDSMap
features.description: Mon computes qdb_cluster_members (ACTIVE rank holders) and leader (lowest rank) at every proposal that touched the fs.

features.name: Map-derived health checks
features.description: MDS_DAMAGE, FS_DEGRADED, MDS_UP_LESS_THAN_MAX, MDS_ALL_DOWN, MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS, FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED, FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS, MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY.

features.name: FSMap filtering for fs-restricted sessions
features.description: Mon filters the FSMap by the session's allowed fs names before subscriptions and read commands.
features.notes: fs dump <epoch> decodes the stored historical FSMap and dumps it unfiltered (src/mon/MDSMonitor.cc:1147). filter() drops standby mds_roles entries but keeps standby_daemons.

features.name: FSMap sanity invariants
features.description: Assertions on every commit/decode tying mds_roles, standby pool, up/in, quiesce membership and compat writeability together.
features.notes: mon_mds_skip_sanity disables.

features.name: Unique MDS names
features.description: With mds_enforce_unique_name (default true) a booting daemon fails any existing daemon with the same name.

features.name: Upgradeable rule and orchestrated upgrades
features.description: Filesystem::is_upgradeable is true when no rank is in, or standby-replay is disabled and either exactly one rank is in (even while it is up and healthy) or no rank is up. cephadm's MDS upgrade disables allow_standby_replay and scales max_mds to 1 (or fails the fs) so new daemons with new incompat bits can be promoted and merged.
features.notes: For single-rank, SR-disabled file systems the 'not upgradeable' filter never applies.

features.name: fs dump of historical epochs
features.description: fs dump [epoch] decodes any FSMap version still in the monitor store (trimmed beyond mon_max_mdsmap_epochs); mds last-seen uses an in-memory history pruned by mon_fsmap_prune_threshold.
features.notes: Historical dumps are not filtered by the session's allowed fs names.

serialization_points.name: MDSMonitor single pending FSMap + Paxos commit
serialization_points.shared_state: the whole FSMap (all filesystems, standby pool, defaults)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Paxos service with one pending value; every change to any fs or daemon is batched into the next global epoch
serialization_points.notes: Unmodified monitor; true conflicts are per fs except the shared standby pool and defaults.

serialization_points.name: Paxos proposal rate limiting
serialization_points.why_serialized: batching: proposals at most every paxos_propose_interval (1 s) unless forced
serialization_points.notes: Bounds latency of every MDS state transition and failover; not changeable from the MDS.

serialization_points.name: MDSMonitor tick policy loop
serialization_points.why_serialized: periodic (mon_tick_interval 5 s) laggy detection, affinity swaps (1/fs/tick), resize (1 rank/fs/tick), failed-rank replacement
serialization_points.notes: Policy cadence of the unmodified monitor.

serialization_points.name: Rank state transitions through the monitor
serialization_points.why_serialized: every externally visible state step must be requested by beacon and committed by Paxos before the MDS and peers act on it
serialization_points.notes: External contract; each step costs at least one proposal.

serialization_points.name: Beacon last_epoch_seen gating
serialization_points.why_serialized: mon ignores state requests from a daemon that has not processed the latest map relevant to it
serialization_points.notes: Daemon must publish map epoch and wanted state atomically (Beacon::set_want_state).

serialization_points.name: MDS-side MDSMap processing under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: mds->mdsmap pointer and all reactions (state change, peer failure handling, resolve/rejoin triggers, waiters)
serialization_points.why_serialized: C++ uses the big mds_lock for all map consumers
serialization_points.notes: Map application only needs an atomic snapshot swap plus ordered reaction to state transitions.

serialization_points.name: Multi-rank recovery barriers derived from the MDSMap
serialization_points.shared_state: states of all ranks of the fs
serialization_points.why_serialized: resolve starts only when no rank is in REPLAY and none failed/damaged; rejoin only when none in REPLAY/RECONNECT/RESOLVE
serialization_points.notes: Fs-wide barrier among ranks; the mon-visible state sequence is fixed, internal protocol is free for a Rust-only fs.

serialization_points.name: Client request MDSMap epoch wait
serialization_points.why_serialized: pool membership and allow_snaps must be checked against a map at least as new as the client's
serialization_points.notes: Only ops whose validation depends on map content need to wait.

serialization_points.name: Compat merge on promotion
serialization_points.why_serialized: promotion of an upgrading daemon permanently changes eligibility of all daemons for the fs
serialization_points.notes: Per-fs effect but decided in the global pending map.

serialization_points.name: Fencing wait before replay/takeover
serialization_points.why_serialized: the predecessor must be blocklisted in the replacement's OSDMap before journal access

serialization_points.name: Shared standby pool selection
serialization_points.why_serialized: a standby can be given to only one fs/rank; selection scans the whole pool in gid order inside the pending map

external_contract.detail: Type 21, header v2: fsid(16) + u32 epoch + u32 len + MDSMap bytes + map_fs_name; produced by the mon (also forwarded MDS to MDS by C++).

struct_v>=4 with len; epoch, flags (as unused m_client_epoch), last_failure, root, session_timeout, session_autoclose, max_file_size, max_mds, mds_info subset, data pools, cas pool, in, enabled, fs_name, damaged, max_xattr_size (ev>=18).
Only entries with 0 <= rank < possible_max_rank and state > 0 are kept: standby-replay followers and CREATING/STARTING holders are invisible; possible_max_rank is then reset to size(in).
Decode fails (mount shut down) if MDSMap fs_name differs from the mds_namespace mount option.
Kernel skips the field as n x u64 while it is encoded as byte length + bytes; non-empty sets make later fields (bal_rank_mask, max_xattr_size) undecodable or garbage (inferred).

Address change restarts session; restarting session reconnects when rank >= RECONNECT; requests kicked when rank >= ACTIVE; sessions of ranks >= possible_max_rank force-closed; export targets in RECONNECT get reconnects; renew caps skipped while rank < RECONNECT.
Subscribes 'mdsmap' (default fs) or 'fsmap.user' then 'mdsmap.<fscid>'; decodes MFSMapUser manually.
Every request head carries the client's MDSMap epoch.

Uses C++ MDSMap::decode; any new trailing fields must stay inside struct length; uses REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION at mount (EACCES), is_cluster_available (ceph-fuse mount only), incarnation changes, max_mds for stopped ranks, export_targets.
One-time fsmap.user to resolve fs name; one-time fsmap for MDS tell commands.
ceph_set_deleg_timeout fails with EINVAL unless timeout < MDSMap session_autoclose.
Boot compat stored (+ forced incompat 7, empty -> v16.2.4 set); every later beacon reaching prepare_beacon must carry identical masks or the daemon is failed.
Feature ids 1..63, mask bit 0 cleared on wire, names present for every mask bit (merge/get_name assert).
Rank holders may only request transitions allowed by MDSMap::state_transition_valid; standbys may not request states (SR may report DAMAGED); violations evict and blocklist.
mds_info.addrs = beacon source addrs; mdsmap subscriptions from MDS sessions are matched by session addrs.
Mon assigns CREATING/STARTING/REPLAY/STANDBY_REPLAY/STOPPING; removal from map or null map (epoch UINT32_MAX) means the daemon identity is gone.
MDS publishes its export target ranks; stored in mds_info.export_targets (bumps MDSMap epoch).
C++ MDS issues 'fs set <fs> allow_multimds_snaps true' with confirm=--yes-i-am-really-a-mds.
Failing a rank holder blocklists its addrs (mon_mds_blocklist_interval) and records last_failure_osd_epoch; replacements wait for that OSDMap epoch.
mgr subscribes fsmap and exposes FSMap::dump layout (filesystems[].mdsmap.info gid_* records with state strings, flags_state, etc.) to modules; mds metadata from boot beacon sys_info.
Subscribes fsmap and reads Filesystem mirror_info peers.

fs new/rm/fail/reset/set/compat/required_client_features/add_data_pool/rm_data_pool/set-default/rename/swap/mirror, mds fail/repaired/rm/rmfailed/freeze/set_state/compat; preconditions and errors as documented.

external_contract.item: MDS messenger entity name equals rank
external_contract.detail: libcephfs takes the sending rank of session, reply, forward, caps, lease, snap and quota messages from m->get_source().num(); with msgr2 that is the server's ServerIdent gid = MDS messenger myname num, which the C++ MDS sets to mds.<rank> on every state change of a rank holder (mds.<gid> while standby-replay). The kernel maps messages through con->private and checks only the peer entity type.

check_sub serves an MDS map (own fs map or standby null map) only to sessions whose entity type is MDS and whose addrs equal a stored mds_info.addrs; beacons need mon cap 'mds x' and a source address with a port.

rust_implications.topic: Compat-based isolation from C++ MDS daemons
rust_implications.implication: The only hard isolation is CompatSet math. A Rust MDS should advertise an incompat set that (a) lacks at least one bit present in every C++ fs compat (e.g. id 1 'base v0.20') so it never passes writeable() for a C++ fs, and (b) contains a private bit (id 13..63) that C++ daemons lack so they never pass writeable() for a Rust fs. The Rust fs compat must then be prepared with 'fs compat <fs> rm_incompat/add_incompat' while no rank is up so that it equals the Rust advertised masks (needed when the fs is not upgradeable).

rust_implications.topic: Never be a superset of a C++ fs compat
rust_implications.implication: If the Rust daemon advertised all C++ bits plus its own, the mon could promote it into an upgradeable C++ fs (e.g. single failed rank, SR disabled) and permanently merge the Rust bit into that fs compat, locking out all C++ daemons and pointing the Rust daemon at a C++ journal.

The mon force-inserts incompat 7 into the stored daemon compat; beacons must carry identical masks, so the Rust MDS must include feature 7 in its advertised incompat set (name can be anything) or it will be failed at its first state-changing beacon.
Encode masks with bit 0 cleared, only ids 1..63, a name for every bit; never change the advertised compat within one daemon lifetime (a change requires a new boot/gid).

rust_implications.topic: Safe creation of a Rust fs in a shared cluster
rust_implications.implication: fs new assigns standbys immediately and ignores joinable=false; to avoid a C++ standby grabbing a new Rust fs, create it with '--set down true' (max_mds 0) or '--recover', set the fs compat, then bring it up; mds_join_fs plus refuse_standby_for_another_fs only add a soft preference layer (host anti-affinity can outrank join_fs matches).

Per-subvolume shards cannot be expressed in the MDSMap; the mon fails over whole daemons/ranks. The Rust daemon must still walk REPLAY -> (RESOLVE) -> RECONNECT -> REJOIN -> (CLIENTREPLAY) -> ACTIVE with each step committed by Paxos (>= ~1 s each when commits are frequent). Use the allowed shortcuts (REPLAY->RECONNECT for single rank, REJOIN->ACTIVE) and do per-shard parallel replay inside REPLAY or lazily after ACTIVE behind per-shard readiness.

rust_implications.topic: Client reconnect window is tied to RECONNECT state
rust_implications.implication: kclient sends reconnects only when it sees the rank in >= RECONNECT (restarting sessions) and libcephfs closes sessions if a rank jumps past RECONNECT unseen; the Rust MDS must expose a real RECONNECT phase in the map for every failover, regardless of internal sharding.

rust_implications.topic: Map handling without a global lock
rust_implications.implication: Treat each received MDSMap as an immutable snapshot (atomic pointer swap); dispatch reactions (state change, peer failure, waiters keyed by epoch) as tasks; keep beacon epoch and wanted state updated atomically.

rust_implications.topic: Boot modes decided by the mon
rust_implications.implication: Implement CREATING (rank never existed), STARTING (rank in stopped: previously existed and cleanly stopped) and REPLAY (failed rank) boot paths, plus STOPPING -> STOPPED (rank must be emptied); with a new on-disk format these keep their semantics.

Wait for OSDMap >= last_failure_osd_epoch before reading/writing a taken-over rank's journal; because the mon may reset that value to 0 when a standby-replay daemon is removed, consider an additional check (e.g. latest OSDMap or predecessor blocklist) before trusting it.
Requests that validate pools (layouts) or snapshot permission must wait for the MDS's own MDSMap to reach the client's request epoch instead of failing.

rust_implications.topic: Enforce map policy in the MDS
rust_implications.implication: kclient ignores MDSMap flags, so refuse_client_session must be enforced by session rejects; required_client_features must be enforced at session open/reconnect and by evicting sessions on change; max_xattr_size must be enforced on setxattr and cap flush.
kclient may decode max_xattr_size as 0 (when required_client_features is non-empty) and then sends every setxattr synchronously; the Rust MDS should make CEPH_MDS_OP_SETXATTR cheap and concurrent.
Publish export target ranks via MMDSLoadTargets during subtree/shard migration so clients pre-open sessions and reconnect to importers after failover.

allow_standby_replay makes an fs non-upgradeable and a follower DAMAGED report takes the active rank down; a first Rust version can run with standby-replay disabled; if implemented, the follower must only report DAMAGED when certain.

Beacon and mon subscription must come from the same messenger addrvec; names must be unique (mds_enforce_unique_name); treat a null map (epoch UINT32_MAX) or disappearance from the map as 'restart with a new identity'.

rust_implications.topic: Settings to honour from the map
rust_implications.implication: session_timeout/session_autoclose (client renew cadence depends on them), max_file_size, max_xattr_size, data_pools/metadata_pool, allow_snaps, inline_data (may be unsupported), max_mds, bal_rank_mask/balance_automate/balancer (may be ignored but are shown to admins), qdb_cluster_* if quiesce is implemented; tableserver and root are always 0.

While holding a rank, the Rust MDS must accept client connections under entity name mds.<rank> (msgr2 ServerIdent gid = rank), because libcephfs derives the sending rank from the message source number; as a standby-replay follower C++ uses mds.<gid>. Renaming happens on state change, so connections opened before a rank change keep the old name.

rust_implications.topic: Do not rely on filter 4 to keep a Rust daemon out of C++ file systems
rust_implications.implication: Single-rank C++ file systems with standby-replay disabled are always upgradeable, so a Rust standby whose incompat set is a superset of theirs is eligible on any failover or affinity swap; isolation must come from the Rust daemon lacking a bit that every C++ fs has (filter 3).
